title: What is known about 1RB---_0RC1RC_1RD0LE_1RE0RB_1LF0RA_1LC1LF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_0RC1RC_1RD0LE_1RE0RB_1LF0RA_1LC1LF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open. The right side is a regular bouncer (3 new cells per sweep); the left side is a sequence of blocks (0111)n and 1k that the sweeps rewrite irregularly. No macro rule has been found.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 30,790 cells have been visited and 22,181 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.234). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.499).

claims.title: The structure of the run
claims.text: Bouncer: the right end gains 3 cells per sweep; the tape is long runs of the word 0111 separated by short junctions and solid runs of 1s, which are rewritten each time the head reaches the slowly growing left end (no regular pattern found).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. No closed rule set has been found; see the README for what a proof would need.

claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LF_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1LA0LE_0LC1LC_1LE--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This page runs the machine in your browser and describes the structure seen in its run.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 30,790 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
bouncer over 0111 blocks with a slowly consumed left side (chaotic)

sections.heading: What the tape looks like
html: At the left end the tape reads as runs of the word a = 0111, solid runs of 1s and short junctions such as 1^3 a^2 1^5. Each visit to the left end eats a few a's from the first run; when a run is used up the junctions merge and the 1-runs grow, then a new a-run forms. The right end of the tape grows by exactly 3 cells per sweep, so the width grows like the square root of the step count; the left end moves out only 248 times in 109 steps, by 2 to 6 cells.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The machine halts on A reading 1 (the transition A1 is undefined). A closed tape language with windows of 6 cells (bbtools.ctl) covers the run but still allows halts, with only a local constraint near the head: the cells left of the head read (outward) 011001, 011010, 011101 or 011110. Nothing confines a halt to an edge; whether the junction rewrites can ever put A on a 1 is open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.234). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.499).
After 109 steps the tape spans 30,790 cells (637 left of the start, 22,043 right), with a density of 1s of 0.72.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.
